text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- The International Monetary Fund could extend a credit to Bulgaria to support the country's fragile currency, the lev, through pegging it to an European currency, probably the German mark, said Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) board member Zdravko Balyozov who is in Washington for the IMF/World Bank annual meeting.

-- The BNB plans to sell banks put under special supervision to foreign investors either for free, if investors pledge to cover the banks' debts, or at their par value, said central bank governor Lyubomir Filipov in Washington.

-- Bulgaria's ruling Socialist Party mulls opening citizens' and firms' accounts in the nine banks put under special supervision in a bid to find the culprits for the grave financial state of those banks.
-- Russia's air consortium Tupolev could supply Bulgaria's national carrier Banlkan Airiles with 16 aircraft by the year 2000, a Russian company official said in Moscow.
-- Bulgaria's Agriculture Ministry posted proceeds of 609 million levs from the sell-off of 15 firms this year so far, a ministry official said.

-- Bulgaria's autumn sowing has been delayed due to the record high main interest rate of 300 percent and the blocking of farmers' funds in the nine banks put under special supervision last week, the Agriculture Ministry said.
-- Bulgaria's private Elitbank, put under special supervision along with eight other banks, could be stabilised, parliament's budget committe chairman Kiril Zhelev said.
-- Bulgaria's government, in a bid to attract foreign investors, has published an add in the last issue of Financial Times newspaper, offering for sale ten of the country's largest enterprises.

-- Bulgaria lost a $25 million credit guarantee for the import of 120,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat after the state-owned Bulbank refused to confirm the credit line on the grounds that the conditions were unfavourable, U.S. embassy official said.

-- The state will sue the First Private Bank (FPB) for the budget funds it has used to guarantee citizens' and firms' deposits in the bank if the court rules against its insolvency, parliament's budget commitee head Kiril Zhelev said.
The central bank opened a bankruptcy procedure against debt-ridden FPB in May.
-- Trade minister Atanas Paparizov left for Geneva, where Bulgaria is expected to sign a membership accord with the World Trade Organisation.
